examples.text: Die Industrie erschafft immer wieder einen Pseudobedarf, und wir geben uns dem hin. Das Bedürfnis nach strahlendem Weiß etwa, das für Reinheit steht.

glosses: schönes Wetter signalisierend

examples.text: Der bei strahlendem Sonnenschein […] aufsteigende Fesselballon mit der Aufschrift „Stoppt Kinderarbeit“ sorgte stundenlang für Aufmerksamkeit und Diskussionen.

Der Tag war klirrend kalt, aber der Himmel strahlend blau […]

glosses: sehr hell erleuchtet

examples.text: Sein Gesicht war braun gebrannt, seine Zähne leuchteten darin strahlend weiß.
[Schlagzeile:] Strahlendes London - In London hat das "Lumière"- Lichtfestival begonnen. […]
„Ich sah in dieser pechschwarzen Dunkelheit ein kleines, strahlend helles Licht.“

glosses: äußerst positiv

examples.text: Steve Jobs: „Ich glaube, Apple´s strahlendste und innovativste Tage kommen noch. […]“
[Designerin und Modeel Sahar al-Rabi:] „Ich will mit meinem Beruf die schöne und strahlende Seite des Iraks zeigen.“

glosses: in klaren durchdringenden Tönen

examples.text: Christa Ludwig verfügte über eine seltene Klangüppigkeit im Mezzo- und Altregister, verbunden mit einer strahlenden hohen Lage.

glosses: mit einem breiten Lächeln, auch: in hervorragender Stimmung

examples.text: Mit federnden Schritten betritt Tom Franz den Raum – sportliche Gestalt, kurze Haare, strahlendes Lächeln.

translations.source_sense_description: Physik: von einer Strahlenquelle ausgehende Energie, Wellen oder Materie

glosses: Any radioactive substance.

examples.text: Any ship nearby will receive a lethal dose of gamma rays, neutrons, and other radioactives.

glosses: Exhibiting radioactivity.

examples.text: As a matter of fact many of our best drinking waters have all sorts of unspecified qualities. Burton water, for example, is radioactive by Beetham's standards up to the ninth degree.
Today, no one would intentionally smear radioactive materials on their face, but in 1933, the dangers of radioactivity were not yet fully understood.

glosses: Dangerous and disgusting, particularly of people or ideas.

examples.text: Even sleazy tactics and his radioactive mouth may not be able to contain this debacle.
It was as though he was possessed of an invisible aura repelling incoming bodies. ‘Look. No one wants to be associated with him now. He’s become radioactive.’
And while Biden’s other nominees have done little to provoke Republican backlash thus far, [Neera] Tanden is “radioactive,” as Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) put it.

If, by some miracle, Democrats hang on to one or both houses of Congress this November, it will be because of Cawthorn, Paul Gosar, Marjorie Taylor Greene, Lauren Boebert and other would-be G.O.P. candidates trying to be just like them — the Radioactive Republicans.

glosses: Radiating light and/or heat.

examples.text: the radiant sun
They in ranks / Sat all, where ſtood the fiery ſteeds of each, / And where his radiant arms lay on the field.

glosses: Emitted as radiation.

examples.text: a radiant face

His sister, Mrs. Gerard, stood there in carriage gown and sables, radiant with surprise. ¶ “Phil ! You ! Exactly like you, Philip, to come strolling in from the antipodes—dear fellow !” recovering from the fraternal embrace and holding both lapels of his coat in her gloved hands.

glosses: Strikingly beautiful.

examples.text: And yet she was ensnaringly beautiful, despite her pride and self-consciousness; radiant and certain of conquest she stood before the man who alone seemed to have neither eye nor ear for charms that had never elsewhere played her false.

glosses: Emitting or proceeding as if from a center.

a crown radiant
